site_name: Amazon AWS PDX-178, Bombing Range Road Campus, 77860 Bombing Range Rd, Boardman, OR 97818
verification: The cited URL is baxtel.com (directory, not evidence, not opened). The other URL in the record, compute-atlas.com (last updated 2026-10-30), marks the facility operational with a 2024 date but attributes that solely to Baxtel listing PDX-178 with a 2024 build year; its other sources are OpenStreetMap building footprints (no dates) and a 2022 Baxtel news item on the March 2022 county approval (a permit, not an opening). So the 2024 year rests entirely on a directory value relayed through an aggregator. The researcher's basis label assessor_year_built is wrong: no county assessor or other government record was cited or opened. No operator, news or government page dating first operation was reachable without searching.

lead.notes: PDX-178 campus approved by Morrow County in March 2022. Multiple directory sources confirm year built 2024 and operational status. First phase is one building; plans call for four buildings total on 127 acres.

site_name: Amazon AWS Hermiston E Penney Campus, 972 E. Penney Avenue, Hermiston, OR 97838
verification: The dates themselves are solid and now have a primary source: the City of Hermiston's Greater Hermiston Enterprise Zone Manager's Annual Report 2025 (dated August 2026, read directly as a PDF) says Amazon PDX138 broke ground in 2023 and received its first Certificate of Occupancy in July 2024; the city's GHEZ web page adds that PDX138 'received a Certificate of Occupancy in July 2024 and is operational.' PDX245 broke ground in 2024 and had no CO as of 12/31/2025. The gap is the site tie. Both campuses may sit on E Penney Ave: city notices show Amazon Data Services parcels at 994 E Penney (variance Dec 2022, consistent with a 2023 groundbreaking; that link to PDX138 is my inference) and 908 E Penney (partition/plat 2023-24, consistent with a 2024 groundbreaking; also inference). 972 E Penney could belong to either. If the orchestrator can tie 972 E Penney to PDX138 (for example from the permit file or county assessor), the year is 2024 at medium confidence (government record, CO plus 'is operational'), source https://www.hermiston.gov/economic-development/page/greater-hermiston-enterprise-zone. If it is PDX245, the site was not operating as of end-2025. The council packets that would settle it exceeded the fetch size limit. Not verified per the default-when-unsure rule.

lead.year_evidence_quote: The first data center in Hermiston broke ground in 2023 and was granted a Certificate of Occupancy in July 2024.
lead.notes: Northeast Oregon Now reported this was Hermiston's first AWS data center, broke ground 2023, received Certificate of Occupancy July 2024. Hermiston is home to two AWS data centers as of late 2026. Earlier planning for Hermiston sites dates to 2017.

site_name: Amazon AWS Umatilla Powerline Road Campus, 80939 Powerline Road, Umatilla, OR 97882
verification: The researcher's 2011 claim fails on site match, and also on substance: the cited page says modules were "deployed," not that they were operating. The pages opened point to the 2011 deployment being Amazon's Port of Umatilla campus (Beach Access Road area), which I infer is a different campus from 80939 Powerline Road; that the two are different sites is inference from the road names, not stated on any page. Amazon has several campuses in the Umatilla area, so a statement about "Umatilla" cannot date this one. No page found that dates the Powerline Road campus.

lead.year_evidence_quote: The Hermiston Herald reported that Amazon subsidiary Vadata has deployed six modules in Umatilla, Oregon. The paper describes the facility as innocuous, bland structures — a row of six shipping containers gussied up with a few doors and vents.
lead.notes: Datacenter Knowledge reported in June 2011 that Hermiston Herald reported Vadata deployed six modules in Umatilla. November 2013 article said adjacent data center was previously annexed and company planned to begin construction on second building in 2014.
